title: Why return type is not enough for overloading
answer: No. Overloaded methods must differ in their parameter lists; changing only the return type is insufficient because a call expression may not provide enough context to select a method by return type. Java therefore treats same-name, same-parameter declarations as conflicting methods. The repository's compiler rule with `int run()` and `String run()` proves that Java rejects this form even though the return types differ.
